case_facts_html:
Situation 1: Expert Ltd. has depreciation amounting to ₹6,00,000 in its books as per accounting records and depreciation as per tax records at ₹15,00,000. There is adequate evidence of future profit sufficiency.

Situation 2: Further, they have accrued ₹8,00,000 towards GST liability for the last month of the year which is expected to be paid off by next month. As per the provisions of Section 43B of the Income Tax Act, 1961 – Any expenditure of the nature mentioned in section 43B (e.g. taxes, duty, cess, fees, etc.) accrued in the statement of profit and loss on mercantile basis will be allowed for tax purposes in subsequent years on payment basis only.

Answer the following questions on the basis of above information.
question_html: In assessing whether there is any indication that an asset may be impaired, an enterprise should consider, as a minimum, the following indications from internal sources of information:

options.A: during the period, an asset's market value has declined significantly more than would be expected as a result of the passage of time or normal use
options.B: market interest rates or other market rates of return on investments have increased during the period, and those increases are likely to affect the discount rate used in calculating an asset's value in use and decrease the asset's recoverable amount materially
options.C: the carrying amount of the net assets of the reporting enterprise is more than its market capitalisation
options.D: evidence is available from internal reporting that indicates that the economic performance of an asset is, or will be, worse than expected

answer_html: Answer: (iv) — AS 28 lists this as an internal-source impairment indicator. Options (i)-(iii) are all genuine AS 28 indicators, but each is drawn from external sources of information (market value decline, market interest rate movements, market capitalisation versus net assets) rather than internal sources, so they do not answer the question as asked.
topic_text: AS 28 — Impairment of Assets (7.3): Internal-source impairment indicators distinguished from external-source indicators

case_facts_html: A Company acquired an asset for ₹60 Lakhs with useful life for 10 years. The remaining useful life of the asset now is 4 years and the current carrying amount is ₹30 Lakhs which includes an upward revaluation of ₹6 Lakhs done in the asset last year. Recoverable amount from the asset is 20 Lakhs.
question_html: At what value the asset will be carried in the balance sheet after considering above facts:
answer_html: Answer: (C) ₹20,00,000 — per AS 28, once an asset's carrying amount (₹30 Lakhs) exceeds its recoverable amount (₹20 Lakhs), an impairment loss is recognised and the asset is written down to the recoverable amount itself, i.e. ₹20,00,000.
topic_text: AS 28 — Impairment of Assets (7.7): Carrying amount written down to recoverable amount when impaired

case_facts_html: A Company acquired an asset for ₹60 Lakhs with useful life for 10 years. The remaining useful life of the asset now is 4 years and the current carrying amount is ₹30 Lakhs which includes an upward revaluation of ₹6 Lakhs done in the asset last year. Recoverable amount from the asset is 20 Lakhs.
question_html: What is the amount of impairment loss charged to the statement of profit and loss:
answer_html: Answer: (D) ₹4 Lakhs — total impairment loss = carrying amount ₹30 Lakhs − recoverable amount ₹20 Lakhs = ₹10 Lakhs. Per AS 28, an impairment loss on a revalued asset is first adjusted against that asset's own revaluation reserve (here ₹6 Lakhs, the upward revaluation done last year); only the excess, ₹10 Lakhs − ₹6 Lakhs = ₹4 Lakhs, is charged to the statement of profit and loss.
topic_text: AS 28 — Impairment of Assets (7.7): Impairment loss on a revalued asset set off against revaluation reserve first, excess to P&L

case_facts_html: A Company acquired an asset for ₹60 Lakhs with useful life for 10 years. The remaining useful life of the asset now is 4 years and the current carrying amount is ₹30 Lakhs which includes an upward revaluation of ₹6 Lakhs done in the asset last year. Recoverable amount from the asset is 20 Lakhs.
question_html: What is the amount of depreciation to be charged to the statement of profit and loss after considering above facts:
answer_html: Answer: (A) ₹5 Lakhs — after impairment, the asset's revised carrying amount (₹20 Lakhs) is depreciated over its remaining useful life (4 years): ₹20 Lakhs ÷ 4 = ₹5 Lakhs per year.
topic_text: AS 28 — Impairment of Assets (7.7): Post-impairment depreciation over the remaining useful life

case_facts_html: A Company acquired an asset for ₹60 Lakhs with useful life for 10 years. The remaining useful life of the asset now is 4 years and the current carrying amount is ₹30 Lakhs which includes an upward revaluation of ₹6 Lakhs done in the asset last year. Recoverable amount from the asset is 20 Lakhs.
question_html: What is the amount of revaluation reserve in respect of this asset:
answer_html: Answer: (A) Nil — the asset's entire ₹6 Lakh revaluation reserve was fully absorbed in writing off part of the ₹10 Lakh impairment loss (per part (b)), leaving no revaluation reserve balance remaining for this asset.
topic_text: AS 28 — Impairment of Assets (7.7): Revaluation reserve fully extinguished when an impairment loss equals or exceeds it

case_facts_html:
ADI Ltd (the Company), engaged in the business of manufacturing of urea, has set up its business in a designated backward area which entitles the company to receive from the Government of India a subsidy of 20% of the cost of investment.

Having fulfilled all the conditions under the scheme, the Company on its overall investment of ₹50 crores received ₹10 crores from the Government in January 2024 (financial year being 2023-24). The Company wants to treat this receipt as an item of revenue and thereby reduce the losses on profit and loss account for the year ended 31 March 2024.

ADI Ltd holds 51% in SHA Ltd. SHA Ltd is a joint venture of ADI Ltd due to a contractual agreement. ADI Ltd is engaged in the manufacturing business and it entered into a joint venture to get synergies in the same business. ADI Ltd and SHA Ltd hold 10% and 30% respectively in SHB Ltd.

As per the requirements of SEBI, ADI Ltd prepared results/accounts for the quarter ended 30 June 2024 and took following positions in respect of following accounting matters:

  1. Training expenses incurred during the quarter ended 30 June 2024 were allocated equally over the four quarters because the benefit was spread over the entire year and similarly some training expenses expected to be incurred in the last quarter have been estimated and equally allocated over the four quarters.
  2. Provision made for donation of ₹5 million expected to be made in the second quarter.
  3. Since historically there has been an immaterial variance between budgets and actuals, depreciation charge for the quarter was determined by the budgeted figure.
  4. Incentives were provided to the customers if they purchase 1 million kgs of urea on an annual basis. It was expected that at least 50 customers would be able to achieve this target before the end of third quarter. No provision was made for this incentive during the quarter ended 30 June 2024 since ADI Ltd believed that the provision was not yet fructified.

ADI Ltd owns 60% holding in ANI Ltd, an unquoted entity. The government has recently announced an increase in interest rates. The increase will cause a fall in value of equity holdings. This is due to the fact that risk free investments offer a higher return making them relatively more attractive. The market value of equity will adjust downwards to improve the return available on this sort of investment.

SHB Ltd took a loan of USD 10,000 on 1 April 2023 for a specific project at an interest rate of 5% p.a. payable annually. On 1 April 2023, the exchange rate between the currency was ₹81 per USD. The exchange rate as at 31 March 2024 was ₹82 per USD. The corresponding amount could have been borrowed by SHB Ltd in local currency at an interest rate of 11% per annum as on 1 April 2023.

ADI Ltd follows April to March as the financial year.
question_html: Will there be any adjustment required in the financial statements of ADI Ltd because of abovementioned event (increase in interest rates by the Government) as per Accounting Standards notified under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules.

options.A: The increase is an indication that ADI Ltd's holding in ANI Ltd might have increased. Hence ADI Ltd would require to increase the value of its interest in ANI Ltd.
options.C: The increase is an indication that ADI Ltd's holding in ANI Ltd might be impaired. ADI Ltd should make a formal estimate of the recoverable amount of its interest in ANI Ltd.
options.D: Whether to make any adjustment or not will depend on the accounting policy of ADI Ltd.

answer_html: Answer: (C) — a rise in interest rates makes competing risk-free investments relatively more attractive, pushing the market value of an unquoted equity holding like ANI Ltd downward. This is a classic external indicator of impairment under AS 28: it does not automatically write anything down, but it does trigger a duty to formally estimate the recoverable amount of the interest and test for impairment.
topic_text: AS 28 (7.3): Interest-rate rise indicating possible impairment of an unquoted equity holding triggers a formal recoverable-amount estimate, not an automatic write-up

case_facts_html:
SBHA Ltd deals in business of manufacturing, purchase and sale of rice. The company has around 56 acres of land as part of its property, plant and equipment which is stated at cost in its financial statements. As per the new business model, 30 acres of land falls in the residential zone which the company is planning to develop residential area as a plotted development and would like to sell the plots after development.

The company does not have intention of keeping the property development as a business on long-term basis, as the company does not have any objective to receive any income in the form of the capital appreciation or rent as per the proposed business plan and the company wants to sell the plots after development (irrespective of the construction of houses on land).

SBHA Ltd has two equal joint venturers holding 50% each, KSJ one of them. The other company is from outside the KSJ Group. KSJ Group has three companies (one of them is KSJ Ltd and two more companies), each of which hold some equity shares in the joint venture which aggregates 50%.

One of the KSJ Group of companies, ADK Ltd, is engaged in generation of power which is supplied to various Electricity Boards. One of the terms and conditions of the Tariff Regulatory Authority and the tariff agreement is that the income tax relating to the power generating schemes will be reimbursed by the Electricity Boards on quarterly basis before the payment of advance income tax.

RIMMI Ltd, another KSJ Group company, is into shipping business and has an annual turnover of ₹1,000 crores. It is required by law to bring all its vessels into dry dock every five years for major overhaul. This cost is incurred to get the vessel back to its seaworthy condition. A vessel costs ₹20 crores with a useful life of 20 years and it requires major overhaul every 5 years. The estimated cost of first overhaul is ₹5 crores.

In the previous year, RIMMI Ltd had impaired one of its Cash Generating Units (CGU) for a loss of ₹100 crores, with ₹50 crores allocated to goodwill and the balance allocated to Plant & Machinery and Technical Knowhow for a loss of ₹26 crores and ₹24 crores respectively. Recoverable amount was not measurable. Carrying amounts at the end of current year after impairment of ₹100 crores recorded in previous year were ₹427 crores and ₹383 crores for Plant & Machinery and Technical Knowhow respectively. Had there been no impairment in the previous year, the carrying amounts at the end of current year would have been ₹450 crores and ₹405 crores for Plant & Machinery and Technical Knowhow respectively. During the current year, the impairment test proves that the CGU is no longer impaired.
question_html: What should be the accounting treatment in the books of RIMMI Ltd in respect of impairment of CGU?

options.B: Reversal of impairment loss should be taken to P&L amounting to ₹100 crores.
options.C: Reversal of impairment loss should be taken to P&L amounting to ₹45 crores.
options.D: Reversal of impairment loss should be taken to P&L amounting to ₹50 crores.

answer_html: Answer: (C) ₹45 crores — AS 28 permits reversal of a prior impairment loss on Plant & Machinery and Technical Knowhow (never on goodwill, whose ₹50 crore impairment is permanent), capped at what each asset's carrying amount would have been (net of depreciation/amortisation) had no impairment ever been recorded. Plant & Machinery: ₹450cr (no-impairment hypothetical) − ₹427cr (actual current carrying amount) = ₹23cr reversible. Technical Knowhow: ₹405cr − ₹383cr = ₹22cr reversible. Total reversal = ₹23cr + ₹22cr = ₹45 crores.
topic_text: AS 28 (7.13): Impairment reversal permitted for non-goodwill CGU assets, capped at the no-impairment carrying amount; goodwill impairment is never reversed

case_facts_html:
On 1st April, 2019, Black Limited received a government grant of ₹15,00,000 for acquisition of a Machine costing ₹50,00,000. The grant was credited to the cost of the Machine. The life of the Machine is expected to be 10 years and estimated residual value at the end of 10 years is ₹5,00,000. The company charges depreciation on straight line basis.

Due to non-fulfillment of certain conditions the company had to refund the entire grant on 1st April, 2021.

On 31st March, 2023, Black Limited received certain indications of impairment of the Machine and the recoverable amount was ascertained to be ₹28,00,000 with revised useful life of 4 years and nil residual value.

On 1st April, 2024, the company exchanged the Machine by paying cash of ₹2,00,000 and new Machine valued at ₹18,00,000.

Based on the information given in above Case Scenario, answer the following Question No. 1-4:
question_html: What will be the impact of test of impairment on Profit & Loss Account of the company?

options.A: Impairment loss of ₹4,00,000 to be debited to Profit & Loss A/c.
options.B: Impairment loss of ₹4,25,000 to be debited to Profit & Loss A/c.
options.C: Impairment loss of ₹6,25,000 to be debited to Profit & Loss A/c.
options.D: Impairment loss of ₹15,25,000 to be debited to Profit & Loss A/c.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Impairment loss of ₹6,25,000 — carrying amount just before the 31 March 2023 impairment test = ₹44,00,000 less two years' revised depreciation at ₹4,87,500 (FY2021-22 and FY2022-23) = ₹44,00,000 − ₹9,75,000 = ₹34,25,000. Recoverable amount is given as ₹28,00,000. Impairment loss per AS 28 = ₹34,25,000 − ₹28,00,000 = ₹6,25,000, debited to the Profit & Loss Account.
topic_text: AS 28 (7.7): Recognition and measurement of an impairment loss - carrying amount less recoverable amount, debited to Profit and Loss

case_facts_html:
Surya Ltd. Has a two fixed asset, FA1 is being carried in the balance sheet for ₹600 lakhs and FA 2 is being carried at ₹300 lakhs.

As at 31st March 2024, the value in use for FA 1 is ₹500 lakhs and the net selling price is ₹550 lakhs. The Company did upward revaluation last year for ₹20 lakhs for FA 1.

As at 31st March 2024, the value in use for FA 2 is ₹350 lakhs and the net selling price is ₹320 lakhs.
question_html: How much is the total Impairment loss for current year for FA 1:
answer_html: Answer: (ii) ₹50 Lakhs. Recoverable amount for FA 1 = higher of net selling price (₹550 lakhs) and value in use (₹500 lakhs) = ₹550 lakhs. Total impairment loss = carrying amount (₹600 lakhs) − recoverable amount (₹550 lakhs) = ₹50 lakhs.
topic_text: AS 28 (7.4): Recoverable amount is the higher of net selling price and value in use; total impairment loss = carrying amount less recoverable amount

case_facts_html:
Surya Ltd. Has a two fixed asset, FA1 is being carried in the balance sheet for ₹600 lakhs and FA 2 is being carried at ₹300 lakhs.

As at 31st March 2024, the value in use for FA 1 is ₹500 lakhs and the net selling price is ₹550 lakhs. The Company did upward revaluation last year for ₹20 lakhs for FA 1.

As at 31st March 2024, the value in use for FA 2 is ₹350 lakhs and the net selling price is ₹320 lakhs.
question_html: How much impairment loss will be charged to profit and loss for current year for FA1:
answer_html: Answer: (iii) ₹30 lakhs. FA 1's total impairment loss (₹50 lakhs, from Q1(a)) is first set off against the ₹20 lakhs revaluation reserve created by last year's upward revaluation of FA 1 (impairment of a revalued asset is treated as a revaluation decrease to the extent of the reserve balance available). The balance, ₹50 lakhs − ₹20 lakhs = ₹30 lakhs, is charged to the Statement of Profit and Loss.
topic_text: AS 28 (7.7): Impairment loss on a revalued asset is treated as a revaluation decrease to the extent of the available reserve, with the balance charged to profit and loss

case_facts_html:
Surya Ltd. Has a two fixed asset, FA1 is being carried in the balance sheet for ₹600 lakhs and FA 2 is being carried at ₹300 lakhs.

As at 31st March 2024, the value in use for FA 1 is ₹500 lakhs and the net selling price is ₹550 lakhs. The Company did upward revaluation last year for ₹20 lakhs for FA 1.

As at 31st March 2024, the value in use for FA 2 is ₹350 lakhs and the net selling price is ₹320 lakhs.
question_html: How much is the total Impairment loss for current year for FA 2:
answer_html: Answer: (iv) Nil. Recoverable amount for FA 2 = higher of net selling price (₹320 lakhs) and value in use (₹350 lakhs) = ₹350 lakhs, which exceeds FA 2's carrying amount of ₹300 lakhs. Since recoverable amount exceeds carrying amount, no impairment loss arises.
topic_text: AS 28 (7.4): No impairment loss arises when the higher-of-NSP-and-VIU recoverable amount exceeds the asset's carrying amount

case_facts_html:
Surya Ltd. Has a two fixed asset, FA1 is being carried in the balance sheet for ₹600 lakhs and FA 2 is being carried at ₹300 lakhs.

As at 31st March 2024, the value in use for FA 1 is ₹500 lakhs and the net selling price is ₹550 lakhs. The Company did upward revaluation last year for ₹20 lakhs for FA 1.

As at 31st March 2024, the value in use for FA 2 is ₹350 lakhs and the net selling price is ₹320 lakhs.
question_html: What will be the carrying value on 1st April 2024 for FA 1:
answer_html: Answer: (i) ₹550 Lakhs. Carrying amount before impairment (₹600 lakhs) less the total impairment loss for the year (₹50 lakhs, from Q1(a)) = ₹550 lakhs, the carrying value carried forward to 1st April 2024.
topic_text: AS 28 (7.7): Post-impairment carrying value = pre-impairment carrying amount less the total impairment loss for the year, regardless of how that loss is split between reserves and profit and loss
